sources_considered.why: Controlled inference tests identify heuristic dependence behind strong original benchmark scores.
ImageNet relabeling experiments identify progress attributable to labeling biases.
Material counterevidence shows that benchmark gains can transfer to newly collected tests.

evidence_items.explanation: Models scoring well on MNLI failed controlled examples that invalidated their syntactic shortcuts. The experiment links apparent benchmark competence to heuristics that do not reliably perform the intended inference.

evidence_items.locator: Section 4.2, An analysis of co-occuring classes
evidence_items.explanation: For the desktop-computer category, this exceeds the study's approximately 30% unbiased-label baseline. The wider relabeling analysis attributes a significant part of ImageNet progress to labeling biases, with only partial transfer to reassessed labels.

receipt.public_excerpt: larger gains on the new test sets.

evidence_items.explanation: Fresh CIFAR-10 and ImageNet tests preserve meaningful comparative progress despite lower absolute accuracy. This limits a sweeping dismissal of benchmark gains, but does not refute the existence of recurring artifact-driven successes.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not measure the proportion of all benchmark victories attributable to artifacts.
They do not establish that entire successful systems lack genuine capabilities.
